items.q: Which set of three factors forms Virchow triad for thrombogenesis?
o: Endothelial injury, abnormal flow and hypercoagulability
items.exp: Virchow triad comprises endothelial injury, abnormal blood flow (stasis or turbulence) and hypercoagulability. It organises both inherited and acquired thrombotic risk.
r: Incorrect. Those are atherosclerosis risk factors, not Virchow triad.
Correct. Injury, abnormal flow and hypercoagulability form the triad.
Incorrect. That set does not define thrombogenesis.
Incorrect. Fibrinolysis opposes thrombosis rather than causing it.

items.q: Alternating pale and dark layers in an attached intravascular mass indicate what finding?
o: Lines of Zahn in a thrombus
items.exp: Lines of Zahn are alternating platelet fibrin and red cell layers formed in flowing blood, proving an antemortem thrombus. Postmortem clots lack them and show a chicken fat layer.
r: Incorrect. Chicken fat describes the pale supernatant of postmortem clots.
Correct. Layered lines of Zahn prove thrombus in flowing blood.
Incorrect. Plaque layering is within the arterial wall, not the lumen mass.
Incorrect. Vegetations sit on valves and contain organisms and fibrin.
items.kp: Lines of Zahn means true thrombus, not postmortem clot.

items.q: Most clinically significant pulmonary emboli originate from thrombi in which vessels?
o: Superficial calf veins below the knee only
Proximal deep veins of the leg
items.exp: Proximal leg deep vein thrombi are the dominant source of pulmonary emboli large enough to matter clinically. Calf thrombi embolise less often but may propagate proximally.
r: Incorrect. Isolated calf thrombi embolise less commonly.
Correct. Proximal leg deep veins supply most pulmonary emboli.
Incorrect. Upper limb thrombosis usually needs a catheter or effort trigger.
Incorrect. Portal thrombi affect the liver, not the lungs.
items.kp: Proximal DVT is the usual source of important PE.

items.q: A solid organ supplied by end arteries develops a pale wedge shaped necrotic area after arterial occlusion. What type of infarct is this?
items.exp: White or anaemic infarcts occur in solid organs with end arterial supply such as spleen, kidney and heart. Red infarcts occur in loose tissues or organs with dual circulation.
r: Incorrect. Red infarcts need dual supply or loose tissue.
Correct. Pale wedge necrosis in an end arterial solid organ is a white infarct.
Incorrect. Lung infarcts are typically red and haemorrhagic.
Incorrect. Septic infarcts contain infected embolic material.
items.kp: Solid end arterial organ plus pale wedge equals white infarct.

items.q: Factor V Leiden increases thrombosis risk by which mechanism?
items.exp: Factor V Leiden alters factor V so activated protein C cannot inactivate it efficiently, prolonging thrombin generation. It is the commonest inherited thrombophilia in European ancestry populations.
r: Incorrect. Antithrombin deficiency is a separate thrombophilia.
Correct. The mutation causes activated protein C resistance.
Incorrect. Excess fibrinolysis would favour bleeding, not clotting.
Incorrect. Glycoprotein defects cause platelet bleeding disorders.
items.kp: Factor V Leiden means protein C cannot switch off factor V.

items.q: Fat embolism syndrome after long bone fracture typically presents with which triad?
o: Chest pain, haemoptysis and leg swelling
items.exp: Fat embolism syndrome classically combines hypoxaemia, neurological confusion and a petechial rash one to three days after long bone or pelvic fracture. Mechanical and biochemical mechanisms both contribute.
r: Incorrect. That triad is non-specific and misses the classic pattern.
Correct. Hypoxaemia, confusion and petechiae form the classic triad.
Incorrect. That describes pulmonary thromboembolism features.
Incorrect. That suggests haemolysis rather than fat embolism.
items.kp: Fracture plus hypoxia, confusion and petechiae means fat embolism.

items.q: Amniotic fluid embolism most characteristically causes which complication during labour?
items.exp: Amniotic fluid embolism presents with sudden cardiorespiratory collapse in labour followed by disseminated intravascular coagulation and haemorrhage. Fetal squames and mucin may be found in pulmonary vessels.
r: Incorrect. Hypertension alone suggests pre-eclampsia instead.
Correct. Sudden collapse plus DIC defines the syndrome.
Incorrect. The presentation is acute and catastrophic.
Incorrect. Bleeding follows coagulopathy and is not isolated.
items.kp: Labour collapse plus DIC should raise amniotic fluid embolism.

items.q: Organisation of a thrombus refers to which process?
o: Ingrowth of capillaries and fibroblasts with possible recanalisation
Detachment and travel to the lungs
items.exp: Organisation replaces thrombus with vascular granulation tissue that matures to fibrosis and may recanalise. Dissolution, propagation and embolisation are the other recognised fates.
r: Incorrect. Rapid dissolution is fibrinolysis, not organisation.
Correct. Organisation means vascular fibrous ingrowth and possible recanalisation.
Incorrect. Calcified phleboliths are a late change, not the definition.
Incorrect. Detachment describes embolisation.
items.kp: Organisation walls off and may recanalise a thrombus.

items.q: Brain tissue undergoes which pattern of necrosis after ischaemic infarction?
items.exp: Cerebral infarction undergoes liquefactive necrosis because of high lipid and enzyme content and microglial digestion, leaving a cystic cavity. Most other ischaemic tissues show coagulative necrosis.
r: Incorrect. Coagulative necrosis typifies heart and kidney infarcts.
Correct. Brain infarcts liquefy and become cystic.
Incorrect. Caseous necrosis occurs in tuberculous granulomas.
Incorrect. Fibrinoid necrosis affects vessel walls in vasculitis.
items.kp: Brain is the coagulative necrosis exception: it liquefies.

items.q: Paradoxical embolism requires which additional anatomical feature?
o: Right to left shunt such as patent foramen ovale
items.exp: Paradoxical embolism occurs when venous thrombus crosses a right to left shunt, usually a patent foramen ovale, into the systemic arterial circulation and causes stroke or limb ischaemia.
r: Incorrect. A ductus shunt does not carry venous clot to systemic arteries this way.
Correct. A right to left shunt allows paradoxical embolism.
Incorrect. Mitral stenosis causes cardiac systemic emboli, not paradoxical ones.
Incorrect. Coarctation alters pressure but does not shunt venous clot.
items.kp: Venous clot plus systemic stroke should prompt a shunt search.
